title: Addition on the integers is commutative
statement: For all integers a and b, a + b = b + a.

formal.statement: theorem Int.add_comm : ((x0 : Int) -> ((x1 : Int) -> Eq.{1} Int (Int.add x0 x1) (Int.add x1 x0)))

evidence.supports: For all integers a and b, a + b = b + a.
evidence.notes: `build_int_prelude` admits this theorem through the trusted `Kernel::add_declaration` gate, which re-checks the proof term against the stated type, so a green run of the command is a machine-checked proof. Measured 2026-08-14: 12 tests pass (a nonzero count -- the filter is not inert).

evidence.supports: axiom_footprint: [] -- this theorem's trusted closure is empty
evidence.checker_command: test "$(cargo run -q -p axeyum-lean-kernel --example int_theorem_inventory -- add_comm 2>/dev/null | grep -Ec '^theorem[[:space:]]+Int\.add_comm[[:space:]]')" -ge 1
evidence.notes: Two independent bounds, because either alone would be weaker than it looks. (1) `Kernel::axiom_footprint` walks THIS declaration's transitive dependencies and prints an empty footprint column -- this is the kernel's `#print axioms`, and it is the check that matters, since an integer law IS still asserted (`Int.euclidean_decomposition`; it was 6 until lane int-remainder proved the `subNatNat` borrow, and the check mattered more then) and Int.add_comm could have reached for one and still type-checked. (2) `nat_axiom_inventory` reports `nat: axiom=0 opaque=0 quotient=0` for the development ZZ is constructed over, so the foundation admits no trusted declaration at all. Counting `Declaration::Axiom` alone would not have sufficed: `Opaque` has no proof body and `Quotient` admits `Quot.sound`, which is exactly the declaration the quotient-of-NxN construction would have added -- the enumeration covers all three kinds and reports zero for each.

notes: `depends_on: F:nat-add-comm` is literal, not thematic: the two same-sign branches of the proof ARE `Nat.add_comm` transported through `Int.ofNat` and `Int.negSucc`. The two mixed-sign branches need no argument at all -- `Int.add` was defined so that `ofNat m + negSucc n` and `negSucc n + ofNat m` are literally the same term `Int.subNatNat m (succ n)`, so `Eq.refl` closes them. formal.statement is `Kernel::render_lean` of the admitted type, verbatim from `int_theorem_inventory`.
